q: Face trauma — what two body areas do you also think about?
why: Face hit → think brain. Head snapped back → think C-spine.

q: What comes before jaw, tooth, or eyeball care?
why: XABCs first. Broken jaw, tooth, and eyeball are not next-minute killers.

q: Trauma patient needs an airway opened. Which maneuver?
why: Open the airway with a jaw thrust when there is trauma or possible C-spine injury.

q: May you use an NPA on face or head trauma?
why: NPA is out. Cracked skull + NPA can go into the brain. BVM would blast air into the skull.

q: When is an OPA still fine on a face-trauma patient?
why: OPA is still fine if there is no gag.

q: How tight do you wrap a bleeding scalp?
why: Wrap a bleeding scalp loosely. Tight wrap adds pressure inside a skull that may already be swelling.

q: Bruise on the mastoid behind the ear is which skull-fracture clue?
why: Bump behind the ear = mastoid. A bruise there is Battle’s sign — skull-fracture clue.

q: Knocked-out tooth — hold which part?
why: Hold the tooth by the crown, not the root.

q: Where do you store a knocked-out tooth?
a: tooth solution / cold milk / sterile saline
tooth solution, milk, or sterile saline
why: Store in tooth solution, cold milk, or sterile saline. Replant window 20 minutes to 1 hour.

q: One eye hurt. How many eyes do you cover?
why: Cover BOTH eyes even if only one is hurt. Eyes move together.

q: Dangling eyeball — do you push it back in?
a: do not push it back in
no; moist gauze, tape so no swing
why: Do not push a dangling globe back in. Moist gauze on it. Tape it so it does not swing.

q: Chemical in the eye. Minimum flush time?
why: Contacts out. Force lids open. Flush inside → outside at least 20 minutes.

q: Something loose on the eye — flush which direction?
why: Flush from the nose outward so it does not run into the other eye.

q: Epistaxis care — pinch and lean which way?
why: Pinch the nose and lean FORWARD. Head back dumps blood into the throat.

q: Halo test yellow ring around blood means what fluid?
why: Halo test: blood in the middle, yellow ring = CSF. Skull is cracked.

q: Torn-off ear packing — cool how?
why: Avulsed ear: moist wrap → plastic → keep cool. Do not set it on bare ice.

q: Penetrating neck bleed — pressure on how many sides?
why: Pressure on the bleeding side only. Never wrap a full circle. Never squeeze both sides.

q: How do you secure gauze on a neck hole without circling the neck?
a: gauze then wrap under opposite armpit
why: Gauze on the wound, wrap under the opposite armpit. Plastic on top to keep air out.

q: Rice Krispies feel under neck skin after blunt trauma means what?
a: air under the skin / cracked larynx or trachea
why: Cracked larynx/trachea leaks air into soft tissue. Subcutaneous emphysema feels like Rice Krispies.

q: Blunt neck with swelling and air under the skin — tight C-collar?
why: Board them if the force was big. Skip the tight C-collar. The neck is already swelling.

q: Unequal pupils name?
a: anisocoria — treat as bad if unknown
why: Anisocoria = unequal pupils. Born that way in some people; if you do not know, treat as bad.
